text:
ken: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to settle operator vs control-plane responsibility for Dedicated pool scaling. TL;DR: who owns headroom and prewarm credits?
maria: Important callout: operator has better locality/fast reaction, control-plane has global view for fairness.
aj: can we split responsibilities? operator handles immediate prewarm, control-plane enforces long-term budgeting + rebalancing.
samir: +1 to split but need a clear API surface. operator shouldn’t decide tenant QoS weights alone.
ken: Proposal sketch: operator exposes /v1/lease-intent (json proto) and control-plane writes desired headroom/credit budgets. operator can bump prewarm within local cap.
maria: That sounds good. Can you paste a minimal proto example?
ken: ```
message LeaseIntent {
  string pool_id = 1;
  string shard_id = 2;
  int32 desired_slots = 3;
  enum Priority { LOW = 0; NORMAL = 1; HIGH = 2; }
  Priority priority = 4;
  int64 client_budget_token = 5; // opaque counter from control-plane
}
```
liz: Who enforces SLA? If operator sees pressure it might preempt. Do we let operator preempt if control-plane budget > 0?
aj: Operator can preempt best-effort within a grace window, but must emit an event for control-plane to reconcile. No silent long-lived divergence.
samir: Also need metric contract: operator reports headroom.available, prewarm.count, preempt.actions in a standard label set so control-plane metrics can do global math.
ken: Suggested metric names: dedicated_headroom_available_gpus, dedicated_prewarm_slots, dedicated_preempt_count_total. Labels: pool, shard, region, tenant.
maria: Agree. Also add operator-level bool: operator_in_emergency_mode so control-plane can escalate.
ken: Edge case: network partition — operator still needs minimal autonomous behavior to keep latency SLOs for critical tenants. Define a small local fallback policy: reserve X% of pool for critical SLA tenants (configurable).
liz: How do we surface that config? CRD? feature flag?
aj: CRD field with annotated rollout via control-plane. CRD: 
```
spec:
  reserved_for_critical_percent: 10
  max_local_prewarm: 50
```
samir: One more tradeoff: frequent reconciles cause flapping. Control-plane should send intent diffs with a monotonic intent_id and ttl. Operator only acts on newest intent_id and smooths ramps over a window.
ken: Good. I’ll draft the intent-schema and smoothing algorithm. Action items: ken -> write proto + smoothing PR; samir -> metric docs; aj -> CRD proposal; maria -> emergency fallback config + tests.
maria: I’ll add a quick sim to check worst-case preempt churn.
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: ken/intent-proto-draft -> staging (ETA 04:30 UTC) :rocket:
ken: Thanks — will ping when PR is up. Anyone strongly opposed to this split?
liz: No objections from me.
aj: Sounds reasonable, keeping operator minimal-autonomy but observability-first.
samir: OK from me.
ken: Great. If nobody objects by EOD I’ll file the RFC follow-up and open the PRs. :+1:
